newsitem.title: JAPAN: JSDA says to take steps against Nomura if needed.
newsitem.headline: JSDA says to take steps against Nomura if needed.

text.p: The Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) said on Wednesday it would take necessary steps if any illegal transactions were found to have been made by Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

"Based on the result of investigations by Japan's securities watchdog, we would take steps against Nomura if there were any illegal deals," Tsugio Yukihira, acting JSDA chairman, told a news conference when asked about a scandal involving Nomura over illicit transactions.

Yukihira declined to comment on whether other big Japanese brokerages face similar scandals. Yukihira, also chairman of Yamaichi Securities Co, took the JSDA post earlier this month when then Nomura chairman Masashi Suzuki stepped down as JSDA chairman over the scandal.
